truthNote: Every card is EXTERNAL evidence about how a mechanism worked or failed for someone else, or an internal preparedness artifact. Nothing here is VORG demand proof. Peer revenue/scale figures are observed claims from sources, never VORG forecasts. Failure evidence is a valid input: it lowers a strategy score with reasons, it does not disqualify (motto: we don't fear failure, we fear unpreparedness).

cards.why: GQ reported a Brooklyn denim-exchange event with intense city participation and cultural energy; city-specific product moments created identity-level engagement, not just reach.
transferabilityConditions: Requires an existing culturally dense metro scene (Brooklyn-class).
Must be RSVP-gated and capacity-capped; unsafe queues and scarcity theatre are disallowed copies.
Only valid after online metro receipts exist; not a cold-start tactic.
cards.tweakNote: For VORG: a booked, capacity-capped fit/try event after online proof — not a street mob.

cards.why: Brand positions products, editorial, community language, and physical experience as one coherent world; coherence is the observed mechanism (brand self-statement, mechanism only).
transferabilityConditions: SKUs, content, and any later pop-up must share one visual/language system.
Community slogans do not convert by themselves; do not copy scale or store footprint.
cards.tweakNote: Firm Jacket + denim + scarf + top share one visual/language system across TikTok, YouTube, and Shopify.

cards.why: Shopify case study reports founder-led trust content feeding a connected Shopify checkout/POS path at mature scale; founder credibility lowered acquisition friction.
transferabilityConditions: Founder must actually appear and carry product truth; mature revenue is not a VORG benchmark.
Pop-up POS claims only apply after venue proof.
cards.tweakNote: Founder YouTube as a durable fit/fabric truth library; short cuts feed TikTok; Shopify owns measurement.

cards.why: TikTok case material describes native employee/creator content connected to Shopify with measured experimentation outperforming polished ads for a small brand.
transferabilityConditions: Platform-reported ROAS is not expected VORG ROAS.
Measure qualified actions (product/size/city), never views.
No fake UGC.
cards.tweakNote: Founder/employee-native clips with kill rules on qualified actions.

cards.why: TikTok case material emphasizes creator format freedom inside a defined brief producing better native performance than scripted brand copy.
transferabilityConditions: Creator freedom must sit inside a signed brief with FTC disclosure, claim guardrails, and commercial-music clearance.
One governed creator test beats ten vague seeding DMs.
cards.tweakNote: Signed brief + disclosure checklist + outcome receipt before any scale.

cards.why: Editorial sources (GQ, Forbes, The Drum) describe founder-as-channel storytelling, one irreducible visual world, and shows designed for social shareability compounding into independent scale.
transferabilityConditions: Needs image discipline: every asset reinforces the same place/story/product grammar.
Lavender-field budgets and peer revenue are not transferable; craft proof must precede luxury adjacency claims.
cards.tweakNote: Make the VORG Firm/Originals world recognizable as a code (3 must / 3 never image rules), not a Provence copy.

cards.why: Forbes/FashionNetwork/Numéro report a founder-duo brand built from small capital where podcast/community/events sit beside product; retail followed online demand data.
transferabilityConditions: Community media must tie to product questions (fit, fabric), not empty content.
Stores/events follow data; reported multi-million revenue is not a VORG baseline.
cards.tweakNote: Founder long-form episodes tied to SKU fit questions; measure waitlist/size captures, not downloads.

cards.why: Official strategy page and secondary profiles describe scarcity as a byproduct of real craft capacity and QC with full-price discipline — not promotional scarcity theatre.
transferabilityConditions: At micro scale this means price integrity and claim restraint, not vertical integration fantasy.
Artificial sold-out with leftover stock is a disallowed copy.
cards.tweakNote: Every fibre/finish claim maps to a quote or sample photo; scarcity only from real capacity.

cards.why: Vogue Business reports DTC-led growth around a requestable hero silhouette (parachute pant) with organic stylist/celebrity demand; US retail followed proven territory demand.
transferabilityConditions: Requires one hero product with proven fit truth; wholesale before DTC proof is the documented anti-pattern.
Do not chase every microtrend or spray celebrity gifting.
cards.tweakNote: Firm Jacket or women's low-rise as the requestable hero once fit is proven; denim compounds after.

cards.why: FashionUnited/Shopify case material describe a named community tribe, limited drops, organic/direct traffic emphasis, and geographic expansion only after online data.
transferabilityConditions: Community needs a name and real obligations (early access with feedback duties).
No paid scale until the circle produces qualified actions; billion-view organic outcomes are not expected.
cards.tweakNote: A 15-20 person VORG seed circle with disclosure and outcome fields before any paid.

cards.why: FashionUnited/FashionNetwork report digital-first growth, drop/pop-up culture, and a temporary NYC base to test internationalization before permanent leaps; founders slowed cadence for quality.
transferabilityConditions: Temporary market tests precede permanent retail; drop cadence bends to quality.
Peer turnover (€33M reported) is not a VORG plan; no early permanent lease.
cards.tweakNote: Brooklyn online proof → time-boxed pop-up → only then discuss permanence.

cards.why: Internal audit of the US-first route found unresolved hard stops (IOR, DDP-vs-3PL, HS/origin, USD contribution, nexus, labels, flammability, trademark, privacy/SMS): the documented way cross-border micro-brands break is selling before these clear.
transferabilityConditions: Applies to any Canadian brand selling into the US; each open gate is a named break-first point.
Failure mode is unpreparedness, not demand absence — clears with evidence, not optimism.
cards.tweakNote: Plan branches touching US checkout/paid stay frozen until hard stops clear with evidence.

cards.reference: VORG internal creator efficiency + weather map
cards.why: Internal synthesis of public priors: nano/micro fashion creators in dense metros (NYC/LA/Miami tiers) offer reachable, disclosure-compliant seeding paths; creator density is documented, conversion is not.
transferabilityConditions: Density is not conversion; requires signed briefs and outcome receipts.
Metro choice should follow the positioning engine's ranked metros.
cards.tweakNote: Seed in the winning metro only; one governed test per creator tier.

cards.why: Nike replaced first-come-first-served drops with raffle-style draws plus bot filtration (also reported by Sneaker Freaker, 2022) because raw FCFS scarcity was being gamed; draws preserved demand energy while restoring fairness for real members.
transferabilityConditions: Only meaningful when demand demonstrably exceeds supply; a raffle with no oversubscription is theatre.
Requires honest communication of odds/limits; one entry per person.
cards.tweakNote: Cross-industry tweak for VORG: use a draw only if a wave's waitlist oversubscribes a SKU's real units; never simulate oversubscription.

cards.why: A social rivalry moment doubled store traffic and drove ~1,000 sandwiches/store/day (KeyBanc via CNBC) — but the chain sold out its ~10-week supply in about two weeks (QSR Magazine), stranding intent: 51% of would-be buyers arrived during the stockout and left empty-handed. Scarcity created the moment; unprepared supply broke it.
transferabilityConditions: Viral demand spikes are not schedulable; the transferable part is supply honesty and a relaunch path.
Stockouts strand real intent — capture it (waitlist/notify) instead of losing it.
cards.tweakNote: Cross-industry tweak for VORG: publish real unit counts per SKU, and route sold-out demand into size-tagged waitlists that count as receipts.

cards.why: Glossier built products directly from community questions (Milky Jelly Cleanser came from a 'what's your dream face wash' post with 400+ blog comments); community co-creation made customers the marketing department with ~80% of sales peer-referred per later case studies.
transferabilityConditions: The content must ask real product questions and visibly use the answers.
Later Glossier stumbles show community love does not guarantee financial durability — keep economics separate.
cards.tweakNote: Cross-industry tweak for VORG: run fit/sizing/fabric question loops on the five SKUs and show the answers changing the product pages.

cards.why: The glitter/bold sub-brand contradicted the parent brand's 'natural, effortless' equity; roughly two-thirds of Play buyers were existing customers, it attracted no new audience, drew environmental backlash, and was dissolved within a year (also analyzed in an Aalborg University thesis on the community backlash).
transferabilityConditions: Brand equity has a shape; extensions outside it fail even with competent products.
For a five-SKU micro-label, everything ships inside one brand world or not at all.
cards.tweakNote: Cross-industry tweak for VORG: no sub-lines or off-world drops in year one; scarf and top live inside the same world as the jacket and denim.

cards.why: An artist's community rituals (ordering codes, memes, merch tie-in) turned ordinary menu items into a demand event strong enough to cause ingredient shortages and lift US comparable sales 4.6% that quarter (per McDonald's via NME/WSJ); the mechanism is borrowed community ritual, not the product.
transferabilityConditions: Requires a partner whose audience has native rituals; a paid mega-celebrity is out of reach for a micro-label.
Supply strain is the documented cost of underestimating ritual-driven demand.
cards.tweakNote: Cross-industry tweak for VORG: replicate at nano scale — a governed creator whose community has its own codes, with real unit counts and waitlist capture.

cards.why: 2.3M units sold with shipments selling out nearly immediately — but chronic undersupply left demand unserved, fed scalper markup, and the 2017 discontinuation caused consumer confusion; Nintendo relaunched in 2018 and 'dramatically increased' Super NES Classic production to avoid repeating it (Polygon, Ars Technica).
transferabilityConditions: Scarcity you did not choose is a supply failure, not a strategy; unserved demand migrates to resellers or dies.
The recovery pattern is honest relaunch with sized supply, which worked.
cards.tweakNote: Cross-industry tweak for VORG: size the drop to the production ceiling honestly, state limits upfront, and pre-plan a restock path fed by waitlist receipts.

cards.why: Influencer-driven demand generation massively outran operational capacity: tickets sold on an aspirational vision with no housing, catering, safety, or vendor contracts secured; undisclosed paid influencer posts also violated FTC guidance and fed a class action. Hype was allowed to become the operating plan.
transferabilityConditions: Universal: every public promise is a liability until fulfillment capacity exists.
Marketing momentum with open operational gates is the definition of unpreparedness.
cards.tweakNote: Cross-industry tweak for VORG: no campaign wave escalates while its gate dependencies are open; disclosure on every seeded post; this card is the motto card — failure we fear is unpreparedness.
